title: Force-close a frozen program from the terminal
summary: Find the process ID of the frozen program, ask it to stop normally, and only if it stays open, force it to stop. Forcing a program to stop can lose unsaved work.

aliases.text: linux app not responding force close
linux program froze how to close it

prerequisites: The name of the frozen program

steps.explain: Find the process ID (PID) of the frozen program. The search matches the program name and its full command line.

placeholders.name: PROGRAM_NAME
placeholders.description: Part of the frozen program's name, as shown in the process list

steps.expect: One line per match, such as '1234 firefox'. The first number is the process ID. No output means nothing matched: try another part of the name.

alternatives.explain: Match only the exact process name. This avoids unrelated programs that contain the same word.

placeholders.name: PROGRAM_NAME
placeholders.description: Exact process name of the frozen program

alternatives.expect: Only the process IDs are printed, one per line, for processes named exactly this.

steps.explain: Ask the program to close itself with the normal stop signal (SIGTERM). It can save its data and exit cleanly. Wait about 10 seconds before the next step.

placeholders.name: PROCESS_ID
placeholders.description: Process ID of the frozen program from step 1

steps.expect: Nothing is printed when the signal is sent. A frozen program may ignore it.

steps.explain: Check whether the program has closed. No output means it is gone. A line with its name means it is still running.

placeholders.name: PROGRAM_NAME
placeholders.description: Part of the frozen program's name, as in step 1

steps.expect: No output: the program closed, so skip step 4 and go to step 5. A line is printed: the program is still running, so go on to step 4.

steps.explain: Only if the program is still running: force it to stop with the SIGKILL signal. The program cannot save anything, so its unsaved work is lost.

placeholders.name: PROCESS_ID
placeholders.description: Process ID of the frozen program from step 1

steps.expect: Nothing is printed. The program stops at once. A shell may print a line ending in 'Killed' for a job it started itself.

alternatives.explain: The same forced stop, written with the signal name after -s instead of its number.

placeholders.name: PROCESS_ID
placeholders.description: Process ID of the frozen program from step 1

alternatives.expect: Nothing is printed. The program stops at once.

steps.explain: Check again that the program is gone.

placeholders.name: PROGRAM_NAME
placeholders.description: Part of the frozen program's name, as in step 1

steps.expect: No output: the program has stopped. If its line is still printed, see the warnings.

rollback.explain: Nothing to undo: the program is closed. Start it again from the application menu, or type its name in the terminal. Unsaved changes are not recovered.

warnings: Unsaved work in the program is lost when it is forced to stop. Try step 2 first, and save your work if the program still responds.
Check the process ID from step 1 before you kill it. A wrong ID can close another program or the desktop itself.
A program waiting for the disk or the network (process state D) cannot be stopped even with kill -9. Restart the computer in that case.
Programs run by another user, such as root, need administrator rights (sudo). This card covers only your own programs.

source.title: kill manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
